rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that items from an outside party arrive at unpredictable times, the participant decides for each arrival whether to take it, and taking one makes the other pending arrivals void: Model each arrival as an intermediate catch event, or as an event-based gateway with one catch event per arrival outcome. Place every sequenceFlow, including the flows leaving those catch events and the gateway, as a direct child of the process element, referencing flow nodes by sourceRef and targetRef. Never nest a sequenceFlow inside a catch event, gateway or task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that items from an outside party arrive at unpredictable times, the participant decides for each arrival whether to take it, and taking one makes the other pending arrivals void

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant must perform a required action a minimum number of times (for example once per period) before the process continues, and a check follows whether the minimum has been reached: Model each required performance as a user task placed before an exclusive gateway that checks whether the minimum count has been reached. When the count is below the minimum, add a loop from the gateway back to the performing task. When the minimum is reached, add the flow that continues the process. Do not replace the repeated performances with a single task or with a timer event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a participant must perform a required action a minimum number of times (for example once per period) before the process continues, and a check follows whether the minimum has been reached

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description states an actor's action on an item with a specific verb (for example, a decision the actor makes about a received item), and a generic verb such as send would name a different action than the one stated.: Label the user task with the verb the description gives for that action, followed by the object it acts on, as the description states them. Do not replace the stated verb with a generic verb such as send, submit or process.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description states an actor's action on an item with a specific verb (for example, a decision the actor makes about a received item), and a generic verb such as send would name a different action than the one stated.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one completed step is followed by several separate outgoing items that are sent at the same time, with no order given among them, and each item is one step of its own: Model the fork as a parallel gateway placed directly after the completed step, with one outgoing sequenceFlow to each item's task. Place every sequenceFlow, including the flows leaving the fork gateway and the flows entering any join gateway, as a direct child of the process element, referencing flow nodes by sourceRef and targetRef. Never nest a sequenceFlow inside a gateway, task or event. If the description later needs all items to finish before the next step, join the branches with a parallel gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one completed step is followed by several separate outgoing items that are sent at the same time, with no order given among them, and each item is one step of its own

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that two different parties each have to carry out a repeated set of updates (a minimum number of times, for example every week) and that the case continues only after both sets are complete: Model the work of each party as its own branch that starts at a parallel gateway. Inside each branch, model the repeated update as a task with a loop: an exclusive gateway after the task returns the flow to the task until the stated minimum count is reached, and then passes it on. Do not model the repetition as one task with no count check. Rejoin the branches at a parallel gateway before the next step, and do not use an exclusive gateway for that join.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two different parties each have to carry out a repeated set of updates (a minimum number of times, for example every week) and that the case continues only after both sets are complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant must perform the same kind of activity a stated number of times or more, and gives a recurrence interval for it (for example 'N items' together with 'every period'), and the activity is modeled as a task: Label the task as one short verb-object phrase that keeps the action, the stated quantity and the recurrence interval as the description gives them (for example 'action N objects, each period'). Do not reduce the label to a generic action or to the object alone, because the quantity and the interval distinguish the recurring obligation from a single occurrence.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant must perform the same kind of activity a stated number of times or more, and gives a recurrence interval for it (for example 'N items' together with 'every period'), and the activity is modeled as a task

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says several activities are performed independently of each other and all of them must be completed before a later step can begin: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow into one branch per independent activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches so the later step starts only after all of them finish. Do not leave the branches unsynchronized, and do not use an exclusive gateway for a join that requires every branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more required obligations, such as one party writing periodic updates and another party also writing updates about it, must all be fulfilled before a later step, and gives no order between them

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an actor chooses one of two outcomes for an item they received, and the outcomes are stated as a choice the actor makes, not as a count or condition on other work: Model the choice as an exclusive gateway whose label is a question built from the decision the description states about that item. Label each outgoing flow with the outcome the description gives for that choice. Do not label the gateway with a condition on a different activity, such as a count of earlier updates or a count of recorded items, unless the description ties the choice to that condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an actor chooses one of two outcomes for an item they received, and the outcomes are stated as a choice the actor makes, not as a count or condition on other work
